facts.statement: Fossils of Pentaceratops were first discovered in 1921, and the genus was formally named in 1923.
facts.quote: Fossils of this animal were first discovered in 1921, but the genus was named in 1923 when its type species, Pentaceratops sternbergii, was described.

facts.statement: The first Pentaceratops specimens were collected by Charles Hazelius Sternberg in the San Juan Basin of New Mexico.
facts.quote: The first specimens were collected by Charles Hazelius Sternberg in the San Juan Basin in New Mexico.

facts.statement: Henry Fairfield Osborn named and described the species Pentaceratops sternbergii in 1923.
facts.quote: The species was named and described by Henry Fairfield Osborn in 1923, as Pentaceratops sternbergii.

facts.statement: Pentaceratops lived approximately 76 to 73 million years ago, with most fossils found in the Kirtland Formation of the San Juan Basin, New Mexico.
facts.quote: Pentaceratops lived around 76–73 million years ago, its remains having been mostly found in the Kirtland Formation in the San Juan Basin in New Mexico.

facts.statement: Pentaceratops was about 5.5 to 6 meters long and weighed approximately 2.5 metric tons.
facts.quote: Pentaceratops was about 5.5-6 m long, and has been estimated to have weighed around 2.5 MT.

facts.statement: The skull of Pentaceratops featured a very long frill adorned with triangular hornlets along the edge.
facts.quote: Its skull had a very long frill with triangular hornlets on the edge.

facts.statement: Pentaceratops sternbergii serves as a guide fossil, marking the transition from the Judithian land vertebrate age to the Kirtlandian.
facts.quote: It has even been used as a guide fossil: the appearance of Pentaceratops sternbergii in the fossil record marks the end of the Judithian land vertebrate age and the start of the Kirtlandian.

facts.statement: In 2016, researchers suggested that Pentaceratops aquilonius might be the same species as Spiclypeus shipporum and considered it a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: In 2016, Mallon et al. found P. aquilonius to be morphologically similar to Spiclypeus shipporum, with it possibly being the same species, and considered P. aquilonius a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Fowler and Freedman Fowler (2020) debated whether Pentaceratops fenestratus is a distinct taxon from Pentaceratops sternbergii.
facts.quote: Fowler and Freedman Fowler (2020) considered Pentaceratops fenestratus to be a distinct taxon from Pentaceratops sternbergi.

facts.statement: Pentaceratops is classified within Ceratopsia, specifically belonging to either the Ceratopsinae or Chasmosaurinae subfamilies.
facts.quote: Osborn originally assigned Pentaceratops to Ceratopsia. Within this group Pentaceratops belonged to the Ceratopsinae or Chasmosaurinae.

facts.statement: Pentaceratops appears to be most closely related to the genus Utahceratops.
facts.quote: It appears to be most closely related to Utahceratops.

facts.statement: Pentaceratops had a frill that was considerably longer than that of Triceratops, featuring two large holes known as parietal fenestrae.
facts.quote: The somewhat upward tilted frill of Pentaceratops is considerably longer than that of Triceratops, with two large holes (parietal fenestrae) in it.

facts.statement: The frill of Pentaceratops was rectangular and adorned with large triangular osteoderms, including up to twelve episquamosals and three epiparietals.
facts.quote: It is rectangular, adorned by large triangular osteoderms: up to twelve episquamosals at the squamosal and three epiparietals at the parietal bone.

facts.statement: The very thick jugals of Pentaceratops do not touch the squamosals, a feature that may be a unique autapomorphy.
facts.quote: The very thick jugals do not touch the squamosals, a possible autapomorphy.

facts.statement: Long spines on the rear dorsal vertebrae of Pentaceratops likely supported ligaments that ran to the front to balance its high frill.
facts.quote: The rear dorsal vertebrae bear long spines from which ligaments possibly ran to the front, to balance the high frill.

facts.statement: Pentaceratops possessed a long prepubis and a long ischium that was strongly curved forward.
facts.quote: The prepubis is long. The ischium is long and strongly curved forward.

facts.statement: Pentaceratops was an herbivore, like all ceratopsians.
facts.quote: Pentaceratops, like all ceratopsians, was an herbivore.

facts.statement: Pentaceratops used its sharp beak to bite branches, which were then shredded by its tooth batteries.
facts.quote: It would have used its sharp ceratopsian beak to bite off the branches which were then shredded - leaves, needles, and all - by the tooth batteries

facts.statement: Pentaceratops lived approximately 76 to 73 million years ago.
facts.quote: Pentaceratops lived around 76–73 million years ago

facts.statement: Pentaceratops remains have been mostly found in the Kirtland Formation in the San Juan Basin in New Mexico.
facts.quote: its remains having been mostly found in the Kirtland Formation in the San Juan Basin in New Mexico

facts.statement: Pentaceratops fossils were first discovered in 1921.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de Pentaceratops se descubrieron por primera vez en 1921.

facts.statement: The genus Pentaceratops was named in 1923 when its type species, Pentaceratops sternbergii, was described.
facts.quote: El género fue nombrado en 1923 cuando se describió su especie tipo Pentaceratops sternbergii.

facts.statement: Approximately a dozen skulls and skeletons of Pentaceratops have been discovered.
facts.quote: Se han descubierto alrededor de una docena de cráneos y esqueletos

facts.statement: Pentaceratops measured about 6 meters in length and is estimated to have weighed around 5 tonnes.
facts.quote: El Pentaceratops medía unos 6 metros de largo y se estima que pesaba alrededor de 5 toneladas.

facts.statement: Pentaceratops had a short nose horn, two long horns on the forehead, and long horns on the jugal bones.
facts.quote: Tenía un cuerno de nariz corto, dos cuernos largos en la frente y cuernos largos en los huesos yugales.

facts.statement: Pentaceratops had a very long frill with triangular horns along the edge.
facts.quote: Su cráneo tenía un volante muy largo con cuernos triangulares en el borde.

facts.statement: The skull of specimen AMNH 1624 measures 2.3 meters in length.
facts.quote: La longitud del cráneo del AMNH 1624 es de 2,3 metros

facts.statement: In 2016, Paul estimated Pentaceratops' length at 5.5 meters and its weight at 2.5 tonnes.
facts.quote: En 2016 Paul estimó su longitud en 5,5 metros y su peso en 2,5 toneladas.

facts.statement: Pentaceratops' frill was considerably longer than that of Triceratops.
facts.quote: El volante algo inclinado hacia arriba del Pentaceratops es considerablemente más largo que el del Triceratops

facts.statement: The triangular osteoderms on the frill are larger at the rear corners and separated by a large U-shaped notch in the midline.
facts.quote: Estos son más grandes en las esquinas traseras del volante y están separados por una gran muesca en forma de U en la línea media

facts.statement: Pentaceratops holds the distinction of having produced the largest known skull of a terrestrial vertebrate.
facts.quote: Pentaceratops tiene la distinción de haber producido el cráneo conocido más grande para un vertebrado terrestre.

facts.statement: The largest Pentaceratops skeleton was found in New Mexico in 1941.
facts.quote: El esqueleto fue encontrado en Nuevo México en 1941.

facts.statement: Pentaceratops likely fed on ferns, cycads, and conifers, as flowering plants were geographically limited during its time.
facts.quote: Pentaceratops, como todos los ceratopsianos, era un herbívoro. Durante su vida las plantas con flores estaban limitadas, y es tan probable que este dinosaurio se alimentara con las plantas predominantes de la era: helechos, cycas y coníferas.

facts.statement: Pentaceratops likely exhibited gregarious behavior, similar to most ceratopsians.
facts.quote: Probablemente el Pentaceratops, al igual que la mayoría de los ceratopsianos, presentaban un comportamiento gregario.

facts.statement: The genus Pentaceratops was established by Osborn in 1923.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Osborn, 1923

facts.statement: A new species, Pentaceratops aquilonius, was named by Longrich in 2014.
facts.quote: subdivision: Pentaceratops aquilonius Longrich, 2014

facts.statement: An exceptionally large specimen was later reclassified as the separate genus Titanoceratops due to its derived morphology and lack of unique shared characteristics with Pentaceratops.
facts.quote: Un espécimen excepcionalmente grande más tarde se convirtió en su propio género, Titanoceratops, debido a su morfología más derivada, similitudes con Triceratops y falta de características únicas compartidas con Pentaceratops.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the largest specimen should remain in Pentaceratops or be classified as the separate genus Titanoceratops.
facts.quote: Un espécimen excepcionalmente grande más tarde se convirtió en su propio género, Titanoceratops, debido a su morfología más derivada, similitudes con Triceratops y falta de características únicas compartidas con Pentaceratops.

facts.statement: The first Pentaceratops fossils were discovered by C. H. Sternberg in New Mexico.
facts.quote: Los primeros restos fósiles de Pentaceratops fueron descubiertos por C. H. Sternberg en Nuevo México.

facts.statement: In 1921, C. H. Sternberg recovered a skull and a tail in Meyers Creek near Kimbetoh Wash within the Kirtland Formation.
facts.quote: En 1921 recuperó un cráneo y una rabadilla, especímenes PMU R.200 y PMU R.286, en Meyers Creek cerca de Kimbetoh Wash en una capa de la Formación Kirtland.

facts.statement: In 1922, Sternberg independently excavated a complete skeleton north of Tsaya Trading Post in the San Juan County Fossil Forest, which he sold to the American Museum of Natural History.
facts.quote: En 1922, Sternberg decidió trabajar de forma independiente y comenzó una excavación al norte de Tsaya Trading Post, en el Bosque Fósil del Condado de San Juan. Aquí descubrió un esqueleto completo, que vendió al Museo Americano de Historia Natural.

facts.statement: Henry Fairfield Osborn described Pentaceratops in 1923 and named the species sternbergii to honor its discoverer.
facts.quote: Descrito por Henry Fairfield Osborn en 1923, quien le diera el nombre específico en honor a quien lo descubriera P. sternbergii.

facts.statement: The holotype is the skull discovered by Sternberg in 1922, specimen AMNH 6325.
facts.quote: El holotipo fue el cráneo descubierto por Sternberg en 1922, espécimen AMNH 6325.

facts.statement: Carl Wiman described a second species, P. fenestratus, in 1930, but it was later determined to be the same as the original findings.
facts.quote: En 1930, Carl Wiman describió una segunda especie de Pentaceratops, P. fenestratus, aunque después se determinó que era la misma de los hallazgos originales.

facts.statement: Nicholas Longrich named the new species Pentaceratops aquilonius in 2014 based on fragmentary fossils found in the 1930s near Manyberries, Canada.
facts.quote: En 2014, Nicholas Longrich nombró una nueva especie, Pentaceratops aquilonius, "la del norte", basándose en fósiles fragmentarios descubiertos durante la década de 1930 cerca de Manyberries en Canadá.

facts.statement: In 2016, Mallon et al. suggested that P. aquilonius might be the same species as Spiclypeus shipporum and considered it a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: En 2016, Mallon et al. encontró que P. aquilonius era morfológicamente similar a Spiclypeus shipporum, posiblemente siendo la misma especie, y consideró que P. aquilonius era un nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Fossils were found in the Fruitland Formation dating to the Campanian, approximately 75 million years ago.
facts.quote: Se encontró en una capa de la Formación Fruitland, que data del Campaniense, aproximadamente 75 millones de años.

facts.statement: Pentaceratops lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The name means "face with five horns," referring to the three typical horns plus two large epiaugal processes on the cheeks.
facts.quote: El nombre significa "cara con cinco cuernos", deriva del griego antiguo "penta/πέντα" que significa "cinco", "ceras/κέρας" "cuerno" y "-ops/ωψ" "cara", en referencia a las dos grandes apófisis epiyugales que sobresalían de sus mejillas, que se sumaban a los tres cuernos típicos de los miembros de su subfamilia.

facts.statement: The frill of Pentaceratops is longer than that of Triceratops and has two large openings.
facts.quote: La gola de Pentaceratops es más larga que la de Triceratops, con dos grandes ventanas en ella.

facts.statement: Pentaceratops belongs to the subfamily Chasmosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Chasmosaurinae

facts.statement: Pentaceratops is classified within the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Family: Ceratopsidae

facts.statement: Pentaceratops is a member of the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Pentaceratops was common in the Fruitland and Kirtland formations and serves as a guide fossil marking the transition between the Judith and Kirtland vertebrate eras.
facts.quote: Pentaceratops demostró ser un fósil bastante común en las formaciones Fruitland y Kirtland. Incluso se ha utilizado como fósil guía, la aparición de Pentaceratops sternbergii en el registro fósil marca el final de la era de los vertebrados terrestres de Judith y el comienzo de la de Kirtland.

facts.statement: Identifying specimens as Pentaceratops has sometimes been highly controversial.
facts.quote: A veces, la identificación de un espécimen como Pentaceratops ha resultado ser muy polémica.

facts.statement: Osborn originally assigned Pentaceratops to Ceratopsia, within which it belonged to either Ceratopsinae or Chasmosaurinae.
facts.quote: Osborn asignó originalmente Pentaceratops a Ceratopsia. Dentro de este grupo, los Pentaceratops pertenecían a Ceratopsinae o Chasmosaurinae.

facts.statement: Pentaceratops appears to be most closely related to Utahceratops.
facts.quote: Parece estar más estrechamente relacionado con Utahceratops.

facts.statement: A 2014 cladogram by Longrich, which included nearly all chasmosaurine species, placed Pentaceratops near the type species.
facts.quote: El cladograma que sigue a Longrich en 2014, quien nombró una nueva especie de Pentaceratops e incluyó casi todas las especies de chasmosaurinídos.
